title: Immersive Service: Characteristics, Challenges, and Pathways to Consumer Agency
authors: Laurel Anderson; Catharina von Koskull; Martin Mende; Johanna Gummerus
managerial_implications: Services that surround a person's daily life, including residential care, can constrain control through boundaries, roles, competing voices, and protocols. Managers should support residents' voice, meaningful responsibilities, and opportunities to challenge routines. The evidence is an ethnographic account of agency in immersive service.
agency_assessment: Institutional routines and dependence can narrow practical choices even when formal choices remain. Provide effective voice, review, and independent assistance.
evidence_basis: Abstract and managerial implications table in the retrieved published version, including desired agency, service constraints, resident voice, and feasible responsibilities; the qualitative evidence has not been independently recoded

title: Extended Reality in Business-to-Business Sales: Performance Implications, Adoption Drivers, and Contingency Effects
authors: Janina Mettler; Aline Lanzrath; Christian Homburg
managerial_implications: Extended reality can improve B2B selling by supporting buyers' mental imagery, especially for complex and tactile products. Benefits coexist with possible salesperson stress. Adoption decisions should match the product and selling context and provide support for employees.
agency_assessment: Vivid simulation can create persuasive impressions beyond verified product performance. Distinguish demonstrations from validated capabilities.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: When and Why Consumers React Negatively to Brand Acquisitions: A Values Authenticity Account
authors: Alessandro Biraglia; Christoph Fuchs; Elisa Maira; Stefano Puntoni
managerial_implications: Acquisitions can damage an acquired brand when customers perceive a loss of its distinctive values. Managers should evaluate value alignment, leadership continuity, brand age, and acquisition communication when assessing integration decisions. The studies support a perceived-authenticity explanation.
agency_assessment: Authenticity language could conceal substantive changes after an acquisition. Communicate actual continuity and change rather than using identity reassurance alone.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Nudging App Adoption: Choice Architecture Facilitates Consumer Uptake of Mobile Apps
authors: Crystal Reeck; Nathaniel A. Posner; Kellen Mrkva; Eric J. Johnson
managerial_implications: App adoption responds to the sequence, grouping, color, and wording of choices. Bundling feature decisions can reduce their individual prominence, and wording can imply a default without formally preselecting an option. Evaluate understanding and feature-specific consent alongside onboarding completion.
agency_assessment: Increased adoption may reflect reduced attention to individual permissions. Preserve clear, separable choices and reversible settings.
evidence_basis: Abstract and General Discussion in the retrieved author manuscript, including the active-choice design, habit cues, decision time, and privacy implications; the full statistical analysis has not been independently replicated

title: All the News That's Fit to Capitalize: How Person Brands Shape Emergent Markets
authors: Gillian Brooks; Ashlee Humphreys
managerial_implications: Prominent individuals can help emerging markets gain legitimacy through organizational identity, founding narratives, and early audiences. Managers should consider how these assets persist beyond the founding individual while checking the substance behind reputational claims.
agency_assessment: Personal authority and founding narratives may substitute for independent evidence. Preserve verification and the ability to question the spokesperson.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Automated Versus Human Agents: A Meta-Analysis of Customer Responses to Robots, Chatbots, and Algorithms and Their Contingencies
authors: Katja Gelbrich; Holger Roschk; Sandra Miederer; Alina Kerath
managerial_implications: Customers' responses to robots, chatbots, and algorithms depend on agent type and task conditions. Findings from one automated-agent category may fail to generalize to another. Deployment decisions should evaluate performance, customer response, and access to human service separately.
agency_assessment: Humanlike presentation may create misplaced trust or conceal automation. Identify the agent and retain meaningful human escalation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Whispers in Your Mind: The Role of Voice Features in Customer Acquisition and Retention
authors: Haifeng Xu; Yi Ding; Yu Ding; Qi Zhang; Cheng Zhang
managerial_implications: Sales-call voice features have different associations with acquisition and retention. The studies identify arousal and perceived competence as relevant mechanisms, while finding no purchase-volume effect. Sales evaluation should distinguish conversion, timing, and purchase volume.
agency_assessment: Vocal arousal and apparent competence can influence trust independently of product quality. Preserve factual explanations and unpressured refusal.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: DICE: Advancing Social Media Research Through Digital In-Context Experiments
authors: Hauke Roggenkamp; Johannes Boegershausen; Christian Hildebrand
managerial_implications: Experiments using entire scrollable feeds can measure contextual spillovers and competition for attention that isolated-post studies miss. Researchers should measure scrolling and recall within the relevant environment and distinguish experimental control from external validity.
agency_assessment: Feed optimization can prioritize sustained attention over users' intentions. Include comprehension, stopping, and user-selected limits in evaluation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Finding Goldilocks Influencers: How Follower Count Drives Social Media Engagement
authors: Simone Wies; Alexander Bleier; Alexander Edeling
managerial_implications: Influencer engagement has an inverted-U relationship with follower count in the studied campaigns. Reach gains can be offset by weaker perceived relationships. Content customization and brand familiarity change this trade-off, so follower count alone is an incomplete selection criterion.
agency_assessment: Perceived personal relationships can make paid recommendations seem independent. Clear sponsorship disclosure and substantive product information protect evaluation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Business-to-Investor Marketing: The Interplay of Costly and Costless Signals
authors: Greg Nyilasy; Shangwen Yi; Dennis Herhausen; Stephan Ludwig; Darren W. Dahl
managerial_implications: Startup pitches benefit from matching language to verifiable resource signals. Passion can help when substantive endowments are present but can backfire when they are absent. Concreteness also has contingent effects. Investors should evaluate supporting evidence separately from rhetorical confidence.
agency_assessment: Pitch language can shift judgments under uncertainty. Verify the substantive resource signals on which the claimed credibility depends.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Curating the Crowd: How Firms Manage Social Fit to Stage Social Atmospheres
authors: Ilias Danatzis; Tim Hill; Ingo O. Karpen; Michael Kleinaltenkamp
managerial_implications: Experience businesses shape social atmosphere through customer selection and the management of shared meanings. Ethnographic evidence shows how these practices influence fit and belonging. Managers should assess inclusion and exclusion alongside loyalty and experiential value.
agency_assessment: Belonging and selective admission can create pressure to conform or conceal exclusion. Use transparent access criteria and accessible alternatives.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Targeting Nearby Influencers: The Acceleration of Natural Triadic Closure by Leveraging Interconnectors
authors: Jacob Goldenberg; Andreas Lanz; Daniel Shapira; Florian Stahl
managerial_implications: Connected followers can help a creator reach nearby users more effectively than seeding disconnected high-status influencers. The evidence combines observational studies and a field experiment. Managers should evaluate network position and actual incremental reach, alongside audience size.
agency_assessment: Network proximity may amplify perceived peer endorsement. Make coordinated commercial promotion identifiable and retain user controls over recommendations.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: How High-Arousal Language Shapes Micro- Versus Macro-Influencers’ Impact
authors: Giovanni Luca Cascio Rizzo; Francisco Villarroel Ordenes; Rumen Pozharliev; Matteo De Angelis; Michele Costabile
managerial_implications: High-arousal language increases engagement for micro-influencers but can reduce it for macro-influencers through perceived trustworthiness. Balanced assessments and informative intent can change the response. Campaign evaluation should account for communicator scale and credibility, alongside engagement.
agency_assessment: Arousal and apparent informativity can alter trust without improving evidence about the product. Disclose commercial relationships and verify claims.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Meaning of Manual Labor Impedes Consumer Adoption of Autonomous Products
authors: Emanuel de Bellis; Gita Venkataramani Johar; Nicola Poletti
managerial_implications: Customers who derive meaning from manual tasks may resist autonomous products. Communicating meaningful alternative uses of saved time can improve acceptance. Product teams should also preserve valued manual participation rather than assuming every task is an unwanted burden.
agency_assessment: Meaning-based appeals could override a preference to retain control. Offer genuine manual and automated modes and explain their consequences.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Why Is It Wrong to Sell Your Body? Understanding Liberals’ Versus Conservatives’ Moral Objections to Bodily Markets
authors: Shreyans Goenka; Stijn M.J. van Osselaer
managerial_implications: Moral objections to bodily markets differ by political orientation: exploitation concerns are more salient for liberals, while sanctity concerns are more salient for conservatives. Advocacy and policy communications should address these distinct concerns and distinguish living from deceased bodily products.
agency_assessment: Values-based messages could pressure people when their moral identities are used without balanced information. Preserve deliberation and explain competing considerations.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Complaint De-Escalation Strategies on Social Media
authors: Dennis Herhausen; Lauren Grewal; Krista Hill Cummings; Anne L. Roggeveen; Francisco Villarroel Ordenes; Dhruv Grewal
managerial_implications: Active listening and empathy can reduce negative arousal in public social-media complaints, even before the underlying service failure is resolved. Service teams should pair responsive language with actual remediation and track resolution separately from the customer's immediate emotional response.
agency_assessment: Emotional calming could substitute for redress if the firm treats reduced complaint intensity as resolution. Track remedial action and preserve escalation options.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Enrichment Economy: Market Dynamics, Brand Strategy, and Ethics
authors: Delphine Dion; Roman Pavlyuchenko; and Sonja Prokopec
managerial_implications: Luxury brands operate across primary sales and resale markets in which consumers seek capital gains. Portfolio and relationship decisions should account for resale incentives, market access, and unequal exposure to risk. Ethnographic evidence helps explain how brands sustain these connected markets.
agency_assessment: Investment and status narratives may encourage risky acquisition when resale gains are uncertain. Disclose downside risk and distinguish use value from expected appreciation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Authenticity in Influencer Marketing: How Can Influencers and Brands Work Together to Build and Maintain Influencer Authenticity?
authors: Barbara Duffek; Andreas B. Eisingerich; Omar Merlo; Guan Lee
managerial_implications: Influencer authenticity depends on how consumers, creators, brands, and agencies interpret the relationship. These expectations can conflict. Partnership management should make creative autonomy, brand fit, and commercial expectations explicit rather than treating authenticity as a single score.
agency_assessment: Apparent authenticity can obscure commercial direction. Sponsorship transparency and truthful product accounts preserve informed evaluation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Revenue Generation Through Influencer Marketing
authors: Maximilian Beichert; Andreas Bayerl; Jacob Goldenberg; Andreas Lanz
managerial_implications: In the studied direct-to-consumer campaigns, low-followership influencers deliver better endorsement returns than high-followership influencers after costs are considered. Managers should measure the full funnel through sales and endorsement spending, because follower reach alone can misstate economic performance.
agency_assessment: Commercial use of close follower relationships raises a risk when endorsements appear independent. Preserve sponsorship transparency and voluntary choice.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Standing Out While Fitting In: Visual Design of Text Overlays in Social Media Communication
authors: Stefania Farace; Francisco Villarroel Ordenes; Dennis Herhausen; Dhruv Grewal; Ko de Ruyter
managerial_implications: Text overlays interact with the underlying image. Large central text combined with dynamic imagery can reduce visual appeal and engagement. Managers should evaluate the complete composition rather than optimize text size, position, and motion separately.
agency_assessment: Attention-capturing layout may make promotional claims more visible than material conditions. Give consequential terms adequate visibility.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: In-Store Advertising with Digital Signage
authors: Dennis Herhausen; David de Jong; Dhruv Grewal
managerial_implications: Field experiments find that in-store digital signage can increase featured-product purchasing, with substantial context dependence and spillovers. Effects vary with product type, placement, and message. Evaluate incremental purchasing and customer outcomes alongside advertising revenue.
agency_assessment: Point-of-choice attention and emotional messaging may encourage purchases without improved product understanding. Preserve clear price and product information.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Before or After? The Effects of Payment Decision Timing in Pay-What-You-Want Contexts
authors: Raghabendra P. KC; Vincent Mak; Elie Ofek
managerial_implications: In pay-what-you-want settings, asking for payment after delivery can increase payment when experienced product value is high. The effect weakens or reverses at low value. Payment timing therefore requires attention to the experience delivered, including in charitable settings.
agency_assessment: Payment timing may increase felt reciprocity or obligation. Preserve a genuine ability to pay the amount the customer chooses.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Customers’ Review Content and Their Referral and (Re)Purchase Behaviors
authors: Ruhan Liu; Wanqing Zhang; Pradeep K. Chintagunta
managerial_implications: Writing a review can change the writer's later referral and purchase behavior. Affective and cognitive content produce different responses across the studied settings. Review requests should support honest reflection and measure subsequent behavior without substituting commercially convenient language for the customer's account.
agency_assessment: Shaping the sequence and content of reflection can change subsequent decisions. Allow customers to describe both feelings and reasons in their own words.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: EXPRESS: The Collecting Mindset: Viewing Purchasing as Collecting Enhances Acquisition Experience and Product Desirability
authors: Elena Bocchi; Adam Eric Greenberg; Zachary Estes
managerial_implications: Positioning a purchase as part of a collection can improve the acquisition experience and product desirability. The effect depends on meaningful progress, active search, and identity fit. Managers should assess whether collecting improves the customer's experience within their intended budget.
agency_assessment: Collection completion and identity can encourage escalating acquisition. Preserve spending visibility and the freedom to leave a collection incomplete.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Golden Halo of Defaults in Simple Choices
authors: Nicolette J. Sullivan; Alexander Breslav; Samyukta S. Doré; Matthew D. Bachman; Scott A. Huettel
managerial_implications: Defaults can change attention and valuation in simple choices, including increasing hedonic selection. Effects depend on goals and the type of default. Designers should compare defaulted and active-choice experiences and make alternatives easy to select.
agency_assessment: A preselected option can acquire perceived value beyond its attributes. Transparent defaults and low-cost override preserve control.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Gaming the Marketplace: Consumer Opportunism and Beliefs about Societal Hierarchy
authors: Shilpa Madan; Aparna Labroo; Constantine S. Katsikeas
managerial_implications: Beliefs about hierarchy can encourage opportunistic consumer behavior through a desire to feel clever. Surveillance reminders and relationship reminders have different effects. Policy design should examine actual behavior and fairness rather than rely on a single relational appeal.
agency_assessment: Surveillance cues can create compliance pressure and inhibit legitimate claims. Explain monitoring and maintain accessible appeal and return processes.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Is It as Bad as It Looks? Judgments of Quantitative Scores Depend on Their Presentation Format
authors: Christophe Lembregts; Jeroen Schepers; Arne De Keyser
managerial_implications: Cumulative versus episode-level score displays can change how people interpret an unusual rating. Cumulative displays may obscure the severity of a deviation. Platforms should provide understandable raw observations and aggregation rules when consequential decisions depend on ratings.
agency_assessment: An aggregation format can distort inference about an underlying episode while displaying numerically correct data. Make both components and averages accessible.
evidence_basis: Abstract and General Discussion in the retrieved full text, including nine experiments, cumulative versus incremental scores, and the distinction between simulated choices and field generalization; no independent replication

title: Consumer Interactions and Peer Effects in Socially Connected Digital Products
authors: Yijun Chen; Yulia Nevskaya
managerial_implications: Peer effects can materially alter retention intervention value in socially connected products. A structural model accounts for endogenous network formation and heterogeneous users. Customer-value calculations should distinguish direct retention value from estimated network spillovers.
agency_assessment: Retention interventions can create social pressure to remain. Preserve independent exit and avoid making peers responsible for another user's participation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Taking a Stance, for Now or Forever: Optimizing the Communication of Corporate Political Activism
authors: Freeman Wu; Helen van der Sluis; Lauren Grewal; Aradhna Krishna
managerial_implications: Communication permanence can signal commitment to a political stance, with responses depending on audience alignment and other evidence of commitment. Managers should align durable communications with substantive organizational action.
agency_assessment: Identity-aligned commitment signals can win support without equivalent action. Make underlying practices verifiable.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Buying Future Endorsements from Prospective Influencers on User-Generated Content Platforms
authors: Andreas Lanz; Jacob Goldenberg; Daniel Shapira; Florian Stahl
managerial_implications: Predicting which new creators will later become influential can support earlier endorsement contracting. The rare-event problem and assumed endorsement returns strongly affect the business case. Managers should validate forecasts and contractual terms before relying on simulated profit potential.
agency_assessment: Early commercial arrangements may be invisible to later audiences. Disclose paid relationships when endorsements occur.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: A Comparative Analysis of Frontline Employee Wellness Benefits and Customer Responsiveness: A Social Exchange Theory Perspective
authors: Stephanie M. Noble; Dhruv Grewal; Riley T. Krotz; Carl-Philip Ahlbom; Jens Nordfält; Dipayan Biswas
managerial_implications: Some wellness benefits improve frontline responsiveness through feeling valued and indebted. Food and social benefits show stronger effects in the reported studies, especially in supportive workplaces. Managers should evaluate employee well-being directly rather than assume responsiveness fully captures the benefit.
agency_assessment: Indebtedness may turn a benefit into pressure to reciprocate. Keep benefits unconditional and preserve employee voice and reasonable work boundaries.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Impact of Negative Reviews on Online Search and Purchase Decisions
authors: Marton Varga; Paulo Albuquerque
managerial_implications: Negative reviews can change search paths as well as purchase probability, particularly for functional products and complaints about functionality or service. Retailers should diagnose the underlying issue and offer representative review access, rather than interpret a mean rating as sufficient information.
agency_assessment: Selective review visibility can hide information that would change search and purchase. Preserve representative access and clear sorting rules.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Weekend Effect in Online Reviews
authors: Andreas Bayerl; Verena Schoenmueller; Jacob Goldenberg; Florian Stahl
managerial_implications: Weekend reviews differ systematically from weekday reviews, partly because different reviewers choose to participate. Review-solicitation timing can therefore change observed ratings. Managers should account for temporal selection before treating score changes as changes in quality.
agency_assessment: Selective solicitation timing can manufacture a more favorable apparent customer experience. Report solicitation practices and maintain representative feedback access.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: When Words Meet Visuals: How Content Composition Drives Social Media Engagement for Marketer-Generated Content
authors: Ivy Chu Dang; Canice M.C. Kwan; Jayson S. Jia; Yang Shi
managerial_implications: The balance of pictures and overlaid text affects social engagement, with important interactions involving informativeness, placement, emotion, and visual complexity. Evaluate the complete composition and acknowledge the assumptions behind observational causal estimates.
agency_assessment: Visual emphasis can make promotional content salient while material conditions fade. Evaluate comprehension as well as engagement.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Separating the Artist from the Art: Social Media Boycotts, Platform Sanctions, and Music Consumption
authors: Daniel Winkler; Nils Wlömert; Jūra Liaukonytė
managerial_implications: Reduced platform visibility can explain consumption declines that appear to reflect consumer boycotts. Separating playlist removal from intentional audience response changes the interpretation. Managers should identify the source of demand changes before attributing them to values or preferences.
agency_assessment: Platform curation can shape feasible exposure while observed consumption is mistaken for autonomous preference. Provide discoverable alternatives and transparent curation.

title: How Insurance Prices Affect Consumers’ Purchase Decisions: Insurance Price as a Risk Signal
authors: Jochen Reiner; Julia Wamsler; Torsten Bornemann; Martin Natter
managerial_implications: Customers may read an optional insurance price as information about the underlying product's risk. High relative insurance prices can therefore deter the product purchase itself. Provide objective risk information and evaluate the product and insurance offers jointly.
agency_assessment: An insurance price can alter perceived risk without changing objective risk. Clear evidence about coverage and actual failure rates supports informed choice.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: How Awe in Marketing Communications Decreases Consumer Preferences for Limited Edition Products
authors: Aysu Senyuz; Jonathan Hasford; Ze Wang
managerial_implications: Awe can reduce demand for limited editions by weakening the desire for exclusivity. Message framing can alter that relationship. Campaign decisions should account for the motive a communication activates rather than assume all positive emotions increase demand.
agency_assessment: Emotion and exclusivity framing can redirect evaluation independently of functional value. Keep scarcity claims truthful and allow deliberation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Who Shares Fake News? Uncovering Insights from Social Media Users’ Post Histories
authors: Verena Schoenmueller; Simon J. Blanchard; Gita Venkataramani Johar
managerial_implications: Past social-media language helps identify misinformation-sharing patterns and design fact-checking interventions. The studies distinguish trait from situational anger and test an intervention encouraging tool adoption. Prediction should be evaluated for error, privacy, and the specific behavior measured.
agency_assessment: Profiles intended for protective intervention could be repurposed to target susceptible users with misinformation. Restrict data use and evaluate protective outcomes.

title: Neural Signals of Video Advertisement Liking: Insights into Psychological Processes and Their Temporal Dynamics
authors: Hang-Yee Chan; Maarten A.S. Boksem; Vinod Venkatraman; Roeland C. Dietvorst; Christin Scholz; Khoi Vo; Emily B. Falk; Ale Smidts
managerial_implications: Neural responses during advertisements can improve predictions of subsequent liking and identify differences in response timing. These measures should be validated on new ads and audiences. Predicting liking does not establish persuasion, purchase effects, or welfare consequences.
agency_assessment: Optimizing early affective responses can prioritize attraction over comprehension. Include understanding and informed preference in evaluation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Information Disclosure via Platform Endorsement in Online Health Care
authors: Jiajia Zhan; Xu Zhang; Hongqiao Fu
managerial_implications: Platform endorsement can increase paid consultation demand and prices while reducing free provision. The observed quality response differs from the access-equity concern. Health platforms should evaluate information value, provider behavior, and access together.
agency_assessment: An endorsement can be interpreted as neutral advice despite platform revenue incentives. Explain criteria and preserve visibility of suitable alternatives.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Applying Large Language Models to Sponsored Search Advertising
authors: Martin Reisenbichler; Thomas Reutterer; David A. Schweidel
managerial_implications: A human-supervised LLM application improves search-ad performance in two experimental settings, with gains depending on budgets and landing-page conditions. Managers should evaluate the complete workflow and costs rather than assume an untailored model improves every campaign.
agency_assessment: Automated message optimization can scale misleading emphasis if accuracy and comprehension are absent from the objective. Review claims and customer understanding.
evidence_basis: Abstract in the retrieved full-text version; methods and results not exhaustively assessed

title: Smart Green Nudging: Reducing Product Returns Through Digital Footprints and Causal Machine Learning
authors: Moritz von Zahn; Kevin Bauer; Cristina Mihale-Wilson; Johanna Jagow; Maximilian Speicher; Oliver Hinz
managerial_implications: A randomized field experiment finds that environmental information can reduce apparel returns, with causal-model personalization offering additional potential gains. Managers should distinguish the randomized average effect from off-policy estimates and ensure the intervention does not obstruct warranted returns.
agency_assessment: Environmental appeals can pressure customers to retain unsuitable goods. Preserve return rights and measure regret or unresolved product problems.
evidence_basis: Abstract in the retrieved full-text version; methods and results not exhaustively assessed

title: The Value of Platform Endorsement
authors: Mimansa Bairathi; Xu Zhang; Anja Lambrecht
managerial_implications: Platform endorsements can increase search and purchases for both endorsed and unendorsed services by changing beliefs about overall platform quality. Evaluate spillovers and customer heterogeneity when assessing an endorsement program.
agency_assessment: An endorsement's credibility can spill beyond the evaluated item. Explain selection criteria and avoid implying guarantees the evidence does not support.
evidence_basis: Abstract in the retrieved full-text version; methods and results not exhaustively assessed

title: Frontiers: Polarized America: From Political Polarization to Preference Polarization
authors: Verena Schoenmueller; Oded Netzer; Florian Stahl
managerial_implications: Political polarization can extend to brand preferences and purchases. Brands taking a stance may change the composition of their customer base. Managers should measure these shifts across behavior and stated preference without assuming political identity determines every individual decision.
agency_assessment: Political-affinity profiles can be used to substitute identity cues for product evaluation. Limit profiling and provide substantive information.
evidence_basis: Abstract in the retrieved full-text version; methods and results not exhaustively assessed

title: Choice Frictions in Large Assortments
authors: Olivia R. Natan
version: 2021 dissertation chapter; earlier related version, not version of record
managerial_implications: Assortment expansion can attract customers while reducing purchase frequency among existing customers. The available dissertation chapter models limited information and choice frictions. Managers should evaluate search burden, acquisition, and repeat use together when changing assortment size.
agency_assessment: Complexity can make meaningful comparison costly. Provide useful filters and preserve access to the full choice set.
evidence_basis: Abstract in the retrieved full-text version; methods and results not exhaustively assessed

title: Bad Apples on Rotten Tomatoes: Critics, Crowds, and Gender Bias in Product Ratings
authors: Luis Aguiar
managerial_implications: Crowd ratings can contain selection-driven gender bias relative to professional reviews. Platform design affects which evaluations become visible and consequential. Managers should assess reviewer composition and rating-distribution changes before presenting scores as neutral quality signals.
agency_assessment: Apparently neutral crowd scores may transmit biased judgments. Assess participation and display design and permit informed comparison.
evidence_basis: Abstract in the retrieved full-text version; methods and results not exhaustively assessed

title: Choice Architecture, Privacy Valuations, and Selection Bias in Consumer Data
authors: Tesary Lin; Avner Strulov-Shlain
managerial_implications: Consent defaults and price anchors change elicited privacy valuations and which consumers enter a dataset. Maximizing consent volume can improve or worsen representativeness depending on heterogeneity. Data teams should evaluate coverage and selection alongside participation rates.
agency_assessment: Consent optimization can change the measured preference it purports to reveal. Use understandable choices and test active-choice benchmarks.
evidence_basis: Abstract and Conclusion in the retrieved earlier manuscript, including endogenous data selection and the conditions under which volume and bias can move differently; numerical effects may differ from the final journal version

title: Targeted Advertising as Implicit Recommendation: Strategic Mistargeting and Personal Data Opt-out
authors: Z. Eddie Ning; Jiwoong Shin; Jungju Yu
managerial_implications: Targeted ads can act as implicit recommendations, giving firms incentives to contact poorly matched customers. Pricing and privacy defaults change the equilibrium. Evaluate recommendation credibility and consumer surplus alongside targeting accuracy.
agency_assessment: Accurate prediction can coexist with misaligned targeting incentives. Disclose sponsorship and provide usable privacy choices.
evidence_basis: Abstract and Conclusion in the retrieved author manuscript, including exogenous versus endogenous prices and equilibrium assumptions; a theoretical mechanism, not an estimated frequency of mistargeting
